methodological_questions: Can 'travels better' be operationalised as a measurable portability contrast between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper roles?
Is n=24 units enough to detect a cut-heavy versus drive-heavy difference in portability?
How are cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers classified from play-type records without the classification depending on the outcome?
Does the 2025-26 partial data create leakage or drift when compared with complete 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons?

historical_evidence.finding: Confirmatory test that lineups covering all three core roles score more per possession net of role counts and talent. Recorded result: M1 COVERED b=+0.0067 (+0.67 pts/100), t=1.35, p=0.176, CI[-0.28,+1.65]; a later final run recorded beta=+0.42 pts/100, p=0.595, MDE80=2.19 pts/100. Failure mechanism recorded as B_powered_null (adequately powered null). Sample: 72 team-seasons in both strata.

Feasibility gate, not a substantive test of the role-effect hypothesis. Recorded: 72 team-seasons with >=200 possessions in both strata; |rho(COVERED,TALENT)|=0.042; aux R2=0.203; rho(TALENT,PPP)=+0.027. 420,993 possessions over 90 team-seasons. Recorded verdict 'supported' refers to the gate passing.

Travel x fit quadrant screen against post-move minutes, usage and destination net rating, n=198 movers. Recorded: corr(delta, dest_net)=+0.077; fit_score correlations negative; net-rating gap between additive and irrelevant quadrants large but the recorded failure mechanism is E_unclear, with in-sample thresholds noted.

Portability confirmatory test (T1): a mover's displacement signature is more similar across franchises than profile-matched destination decoys. Recorded median self_sim=+0.129 vs decoy_sim=+0.049; median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.0050; 173/294 positive (sign p=2.87e-3); destination-franchise CI [+0.0192,+0.0859]. Prereg record gave 296 movers, Delta=+0.0819.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether covering all three core roles in a lineup adds per-possession value net of role counts and talent.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null) with 72 team-seasons; the MDE80 was about 2.19 pts/100, so small role effects were not detectable at that sample size. The earlier estimate (+0.67 pts/100) and the later run (+0.42 pts/100) both fell well short of significance.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a travel x fit screen to predict post-move outcomes for movers.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear. The correlation between delta and destination net rating was small (+0.077), fit-score correlations were negative, and thresholds were set in-sample. Its auto-recorded risks include LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project on a related coverage question found that a 90 team-season design (72 with adequate possessions) could be run with the gating checks (within-team variation, separability from talent, talent control), but these checks were recorded only as feasibility gates.

A confirmatory test on a related role-coverage hypothesis with 72 team-seasons returned a powered null, which indicates that role effects of the size plausibly at stake here were not reliably detectable at that sample size.
A portability-style test (SF19) was recorded as supported with about 294 movers, showing that a mover-based displacement design can be run when the unit count is in the hundreds.
A related outcome-screen (SF-PAP-032) with 198 movers was recorded as inconclusive, with outcome-derived labels and in-sample thresholds flagged as risks.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper roles or their portability. All records concern coverage or travel/fit or displacement signatures, so the retrieved evidence is adjacent, not direct.
Nothing retrieved shows that n=24 units suffices. The closest powered analogue (72 team-seasons) returned a null with a large MDE, which points the other way.
No retrieved record establishes how cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers should be classified from play-type data, or whether that classification is stable across seasons and playoffs.
No retrieved record reports the unit definition for this question (player, team-season or lineup), so the mapping from n=24 to the estimand is unknown.
own_inferences: With 24 units, the minimum detectable effect is likely to be far larger than the effects the earlier coverage studies reported, so a null result would be uninformative.
A player-level mover design (as in SF19) would give more units than 24 and would be the more plausible route to a useful test, if the cut/drive labels can be defined without reference to the outcome.

The 2025-26 playoffs and regular season are partial before 2026-06-21 and 2026-04-13 respectively; using them before completion would introduce leakage and mix incomplete exposure into the comparison.
The role labels (cut-heavy/drive-heavy) are derived from the same play-by-play used to compute outcomes, so unless the classifier is fixed on pre-period data, the comparison is circular.
uncertainties: The unit of analysis and what n=24 counts (players, team-seasons, lineups) is not specified in the task.
The threshold defining cut-heavy versus drive-heavy is not given.
The 'travel' construct (portability across contexts) has no operational definition in the task; the retrieved portability record (SF19) uses a franchise-to-franchise signature that may not match.
Exposure counts per shaper type within 24 units are unknown and may be sparse.
The retrieved records were marked with auto-generated fields and some NOT_RECORDED notes; their reliability was not checked beyond the summaries given.

historical_effect.explanation: Earlier work on a related coverage hypothesis (FAM:SF29) returned a powered null at 72 team-seasons with a large MDE, and the travel/fit screen (FAM:SF-PAP-032) was inconclusive. Together these show that the effects plausibly at stake here are hard to detect at this scale and that outcome-derived labels caused trouble, so the decision moved from a plain proceed to do_not_proceed as posed, with a recommendation to re-scope.

blocking_constraints.text: 24 units is far below the 72-team-season scale where a related role test returned a powered null with MDE about 2.19 pts/100; the expected effect is likely below the detectable range.
Cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper exposure per unit may be too sparse to estimate role-specific portability.
Role labels come from the same play-by-play as outcomes, so classification can encode the outcome.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work covers role coverage (SF29, SF-PAP-009; powered null), travel/fit screening (SF-PAP-032; inconclusive) and portability of displacement signatures (SF19; supported). None tests cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers, so the specific question is not answered, though portability has been studied in an adjacent form.

risks.text: n=24 units gives low power; a null would be uninformative and a significant result would likely be inflated.
Few units may contain enough cut-heavy or drive-heavy possessions to estimate role-specific effects.
Play-type classification from derived play-by-play records may be noisy and unstable across seasons.
Role labels and outcome measures both come from play-by-play; the classification must be fixed before outcomes are examined.
Using partial 2025-26 regular-season or playoff data, or using full-season role labels to predict within-season outcomes, would leak future information.
Talent, team context and minutes distribution can confound a cut-heavy versus drive-heavy comparison.
Play style and rule or tracking changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can shift role definitions over time.
SF19 was recorded with a placebo-style decoy design; portability results may depend on how decoys are matched.
Several role definitions, thresholds and outcomes give many comparisons; without correction, a spurious portability difference is likely.
Misattributed play types or shooter identities in the play-by-play would misclassify shapers.

design.estimand: Difference in portability (out-of-context performance or signature similarity retention) between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, as a contrast of predefined role-share classes.
design.unit: Shaper-season (player-level mover records), not the 24-unit count, if the unit count cannot be raised; each unit defined before analysis.
design.sample: Not feasible at n=24 as posed. Minimum viable: all shapers with defined role shares across 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete seasons (regular season and playoffs), with 2025-26 only after completion (regular season from 2026-04-13, playoffs from 2026-06-21).
design.power: Pre-register an MDE before analysis; if the MDE exceeds the plausible effect range or the number of units is below the level of the SF29 run (72 units), do not run the confirmatory test.
design.controls: Talent proxy, team context, minutes share and usage, with role classes fixed on pre-period data; outcomes measured in a later window than the role labels.
design.falsification: Placebo role labels (shuffled within player) and a decoy-matched comparison as in SF19; a null on placebo labels is required before a positive result counts.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (cut-heavy minus drive-heavy portability), with any secondary definitions reported as exploratory and corrected.
design.decision_rule: Positive only if the primary contrast's CI excludes zero at the pre-registered threshold, survives the placebo test, and the sample meets the pre-registered MDE; otherwise report as uninformative or null.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs (complete); 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13 and playoffs only after 2026-06-21; freeze all role definitions before 2025-26 data are used.

methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper roles be operationalized from play-by-play and derived play-type records?
What risks arise when comparing role transfer across seasons and playoffs with small unit counts?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
